title: “Rādha, whatever desire, lust, delight, craving there is for form — abandon it. Thus that form will be abandoned, cut off at the root, made…
content: “Rādha, whatever desire, lust, delight, craving there is for form — abandon it. Thus that form will be abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, made non-existent, so that it cannot arise again in the future. Regarding feeling … perception … formations … Rādha, whatever desire, lust, delight, craving there is for consciousness — abandon it. Thus that consciousness will be abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, made non-existent, so that it cannot arise again in the future.”

title: “‘Visible here and now, visible here and now (sanditthiko),’ venerable sir, is said. To what extent, venerable sir, is the Dhamma visible here and now,…
content: “‘Visible here and now, visible here and now (sanditthiko),’ venerable sir, is said. To what extent, venerable sir, is the Dhamma visible here and now, immediate, inviting inspection, leading onward, to be directly experienced by the wise?” - “Here, Upavāna, having seen a form with the eye, a monk experiences the form but does not experience lust for the form, and there is no inner lust for forms. He knows: ‘There is no inner lust for forms in me.’ As long as, Upavāna, having seen a form with the eye, a monk experiences the form but does not experience lust for the form, and there is no inner lust for forms — he knows that — thus, Upavāna, the Dhamma is visible here and now, immediate, inviting inspection, leading onward, to be directly experienced by the wise.”

title: Elder Hatthārohaputta: “This mind formerly wandered Wherever it wished, as it liked, as it pleased. Now I will restrain it thoroughly With wise reflection, As…
content:
Elder Hatthārohaputta:
“This mind formerly wandered
Wherever it wished, as it liked, as it pleased.
Now I will restrain it thoroughly
With wise reflection,
As a driver with a hook
Restrains a rutting elephant.”

title: “And how, monks, is a monk ‘washed clean’? He has washed away evil, unwholesome states that are defiling, leading to renewed existence, fearful, producing painful…
content: “And how, monks, is a monk ‘washed clean’? He has washed away evil, unwholesome states that are defiling, leading to renewed existence, fearful, producing painful results, leading to future birth, aging, and death. Thus, monks, a monk is ‘washed clean.’”

title: “Monks, just as a young man or woman, youthful, fond of adornment, would be distressed, ashamed, and disgusted if the carcass of a snake, a…
content: “Monks, just as a young man or woman, youthful, fond of adornment, would be distressed, ashamed, and disgusted if the carcass of a snake, a dog, or a human were hung around their neck; so too, monks, that monk, examining the peril in those thoughts … the mind becomes steadied, settled, unified, and concentrated.”

title: “Monks, what are the defilements that should be abandoned by restraint? Here, a monk, reflecting wisely, lives with the restraint of the eye faculty. Monks,…
content: “Monks, what are the defilements that should be abandoned by restraint? Here, a monk, reflecting wisely, lives with the restraint of the eye faculty. Monks, if he lives without restraining the eye faculty, harmful, feverish defilements might arise. If he restrains the eye faculty, those harmful, feverish defilements are no more. These, monks, are called the defilements that should be abandoned by restraint.”

title: “Fear, monks, is a synonym for sensual pleasures. Suffering, monks, is a synonym for sensual pleasures. Disease, monks, is a synonym for sensual pleasures. A…
content:
“Fear, monks, is a synonym for sensual pleasures. Suffering, monks, is a synonym for sensual pleasures. Disease, monks, is a synonym for sensual pleasures. A boil, monks, is a synonym for sensual pleasures. A dart, monks, is a synonym for sensual pleasures. Bondage, monks, is a synonym for sensual pleasures. Mud, monks, is a synonym for sensual pleasures. A womb, monks, is a synonym for sensual pleasures.
How, monks, is fear a synonym for sensual pleasures? Because those who are infected by sensual desire, bound by sensual lust, are not freed from fear in the present life, not freed from fear in the future — therefore fear is a synonym for sensual pleasures.”

title: Elder Nun Sundarī Nandā: Nandā, look at this body — Diseased, impure, stinking. Develop the mind on foulness, One-pointed, well-concentrated. As this body, so that…
content:
Elder Nun Sundarī Nandā:

Nandā, look at this body —
Diseased, impure, stinking.
Develop the mind on foulness,
One-pointed, well-concentrated.

As this body, so that body —
As that body, so this body —
Foul, rotting —
Only fools delight in it.

Thus contemplate this body,
Day and night without fatigue.
With your own wisdom,
Therefore escape.
With your own wisdom,
Escape pride in beauty,
And see truly
What fools see.

This city is built of bones,
Plastered with flesh and blood.
Within dwell aging and death,
Conceit and hypocrisy.

Without heedlessness,
Rightly contemplate that body —
The true nature of this body
Is seen inside and out.
I am disenchanted with the body,
My mind is dispassionate.
Without heedlessness, free from bonds,
I am at peace, stilled.

title: “Monks, just as a defiled, dust-covered cloth, when a dyer dips it in this or that dye – blue, yellow, red, or purple – will…
content: “Monks, just as a defiled, dust-covered cloth, when a dyer dips it in this or that dye – blue, yellow, red, or purple – will take the dye poorly and be unclean. Why is that? Because the cloth is not clean. So too, monks, a foul destination awaits a defiled mind. Monks, just as a clean, bright cloth, when a dyer dips it in this or that dye – blue, yellow, red, or purple – will take the dye well and be clean. Why is that? Because the cloth is clean. So too, monks, a good destination awaits an undefiled mind.”

title: “Monk, whoever thinks about form is bound by Māra. Whoever does not think about form is freed from the Evil One. Whoever thinks about feeling…
content: “Monk, whoever thinks about form is bound by Māra. Whoever does not think about form is freed from the Evil One. Whoever thinks about feeling … perception … formations … consciousness is bound by Māra. Whoever does not think about consciousness is freed from the Evil One. This brief saying of mine, monk, should be understood in detail.”
